evidence.role: drowsiness with spontaneous awakening = Grade 1 consciousness criterion (A3), Day 4
evidence.quote: drowsy through the afternoon, dozing off between sentences, but awakens spontaneously each time without being spoken to or touched
No sedatives, antihistamines or opioids given at any time this admission.
Assessment: neurotoxicity with reduced alertness despite a normal ICE.
No focal weakness, no seizure activity.

derivation.onset: Section 3.3 footnote / A3: 'awakens spontaneously' counts as Grade 1 when drowsiness is documented, as here, with an explicit absence of sedating drugs. This Day 4 observation (2032-09-25) is the earliest qualifying one, although ICE was 10/10. Record Day 4 equals documented Day 4, so 7.7.
derivation.max_grade: The worst findings are Grade 1 (drowsy with spontaneous awakening Day 4, ICE 9/10 Day 5). No Grade 2 or higher criterion appears. Record Grade 1 equals documented Grade 1, so 7.7.

ambiguity_notes: The onset depends on A3 (drowsiness documented with spontaneous awakening counts as Grade 1 despite ICE 10/10). If a clinician reviewer did not accept it, the first Grade 1 finding would be ICE 9/10 on Day 5 and the Day 4 note would be a formal Grade 0 assessment at ICE 10/10, giving 7.1 with a signed difference of -1 (record Day 4, documented Day 5). Under the stated rule A3 applies, so 7.7. No consciousness wording is ambiguous: the note explicitly says 'without being spoken to or touched', which excludes the 'awakens to voice' category.
